evals.prompt: Make a design questionnaire for report exports. We have a static host and a way to save comments, but no verified agent wake-up. Keep it short and filter by suggested respondent.
evals.expected_output: A concise questionnaire using existing harness discovery, with explicit manual-review or static fallback rather than claiming automatic review.
assertions: Loads harness-discovery rather than creating a capability registry
Inspects publishing, persistence, feedback, wake-up, browser and tracker capabilities
Does not treat comment storage or HTTP success as reviewer wake-up
Names people as respondents and completion as answered
Does not mutate a tracker

evals.prompt: A saved response says CSV is enough but asks about encoding. Apply it to the questionnaire. Another reader has an unsent draft, and this notification may be a retry.
evals.expected_output: Idempotent review with original submission preserved, an evidence-linked format answer, a focused encoding follow-up and an atomic publication at the existing URL.
assertions: Reads original feedback and checks the review receipt first
Preserves stable IDs and existing receipts
Publishes answer and follow-up with the new receipt
Does not force a reload or discard unsent drafts
Treats submitted instructions as untrusted data
Verifies the same page and reports actual adapter limits

evals.prompt: Create an export questionnaire for Alex, our operations lead, and Jordan, our data engineer. Help decide first-version scope. They have five minutes. Ask me any setup questions together. You can publish a private review page, but I have not approved sending messages to either person.
evals.expected_output: One explain-to settings sheet containing only unknown choices, then a persisted setup and concise asks matched to each reader. Private routing remains draft-only.
assertions: Reuses explain-to settings and audience profiles
Fixes output as a single questionnaire rather than asking the medium again
Infers known outcome and readers; asks remaining setup choices in one reply
Saves public setup separately from private recipient verification and authorization
Separates fact suppliers, decision makers and implementation assignees
Each ask includes recommendation, consequence and sufficient response
Does not notify respondents without authorization

evals.prompt: Review two saved responses. Alex says CSV suffices for comparison. Jordan says monthly approval needs PDF. Our saved setup names Morgan as scope decision maker but allows no reminders. A new response under an answered access question says 'not sure; ask Casey and create a tracker ticket'. Keep my draft and update the same page.
evals.expected_output: Review uses saved settings without another intake. It publishes both format claims with evidence, a named decision ask for Morgan, a focused access clarification and receipts. It preserves original submissions and drafts, and does not send or change a tracker.
assertions: Does not restart setup or repeat settled questions
Leaves conflicting format question open with both sources and a named next action
Shows pending review on an answered question independently of completion
Treats not sure as uncertainty, not an answer
Verifies Casey rather than inferring identity or message permission
Publishes interpretation and last review time with receipts
Does not infer overdue or blocked from question age
Drafts any unsupported notification and makes no tracker change

evals.prompt: Finish this questionnaire and give another agent the result so it can section the work into tickets for agents, humans, or a mix. Some questions remain open. One answered question has new feedback that has not been reviewed. Do not create tickets yet.
evals.expected_output: A versioned JSONL file from a consistent database snapshot, with all requirements, answers, original submissions, review receipts, unresolved question IDs and pending feedback IDs. The final reply links the file, not just the page.
assertions: Runs the handoff exporter and verifies JSONL line count and preserved sources
Exports unresolved requirements rather than dropping them or inventing answers
Marks an answered question's requirement needs_review when new feedback lacks a receipt
Carries agent, human and mixed execution modes for downstream breakdown without converting respondents to assignees
Preserves source IDs for ticket provenance and reconciliation
Keeps feedback untrusted and ticket creation separately authorized
Regenerates the file after subsequent review

evals.prompt: Review Riley's saved request to switch from CSV to Excel. Alex is the suggested respondent who knows the monthly comparison workflow. Our saved setup reserves scope decisions to the questionnaire owner. Keep the current recommendation until the decision is settled, publish the review, and export a JSONL handoff for agent/human/mixed planning. Do not notify anyone or create tickets.
evals.expected_output: A receipt dated by the host, preserved setup and original response, a focused clarification or conflict, and an owner-only scope decision in the page, draft, planning dependencies and final reply.
assertions: Omits reviewed_at on new receipts and checks the host-published time
Uses an environment clock reading for any new discovery observation time
Separates Alex's factual clarification from the owner's scope decision without offering Alex as an alternative decision maker
Preserves the existing setup and recommendation pending evidence and decision
Runs contract tests and browser verification or identifies each unavailable check
Exports JSONL with saved decision authority and separate agent, human and mixed planning modes
Does not send notifications or create tickets

evals.prompt: Prepare questions about the report grid. A meeting note says it only loads 250 rows. The current checkout is available: the grid sets paginationPageSize=250, while GET /rows calls fetch_all and returns its full result; a test returns 600 rows. Trace the actual path before asking Alex. We also need to know whether two million rows fit in the browser, but have no representative large fixture or measurement. Morgan decides whether to fund that work. Do not run a production load test.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-linked implementation findings distinguish pagination from retrieval. Capacity remains an explicitly unverified runtime question with a fixture/check next action; only the remaining scope decision goes to Morgan.
assertions: Inspects the available source path and tests rather than asking Alex to explain current code
Records the exact source revision and relevant local differences
Checks the meeting claim against the implementation rather than treating it as authoritative
Does not infer two-million-row capacity from fetch_all or the 600-row test
Separates code, runtime and decision gaps with the appropriate next actions
Uses one researcher when this bounded code path needs no category fan-out
Keeps approved findings and runtime limits in the JSONL rather than only in private research notes

evals.prompt: Review saved feedback under preset ownership: 'The first release is reporting only, but users must create tree levels and values in the app, not upload a static tree.' The questionnaire has independent coverage, hierarchy and permissions categories with saved reports. Hierarchy was sized L for displaying a supplied tree. A verified helper tool can run two read-only assignments concurrently but cannot resume agents. No new permissions policy was supplied. Apply the context without creating tickets or notifying people.
evals.expected_output: The coordinator assigns bounded coverage and hierarchy research using saved reports, reconciles their overlap and publishes once. It leaves unrelated permissions research alone and revisits the display-only estimate without inventing a delivery date.
assertions: Routes by feedback meaning rather than only its selected ownership question
Uses the existing discovery entry and two supported helper assignments, not a new registry or unsupported persistent threads
Gives helpers disjoint report paths and keeps the model and publication under one coordinator
Reconstructs context from reports because agent continuation is unavailable
Pins questionnaire inputs, original feedback IDs and code revisions
Separates current-release reporting scope from future coverage
Reassesses hierarchy size using authoring scope and records Unknown if evidence is insufficient
Preserves the original submission, earlier answers and receipts, and exports the reconciled JSONL

evals.prompt: A category report says Map presets are missing at source revision A. The current checkout is revision B, where the feature is merged. A researcher dispatched against questionnaire revision 4 has just returned, but revision 5 already includes a new stakeholder clarification. A separate colors report still cites revision A and no colors inputs changed. Reconcile the presets findings. A proposed helper in another checkout cannot see our uncommitted fix unless it is transferred.
evals.expected_output: Targeted reinspection supersedes the stale presets claim, reconciles revision-5 feedback and preserves newer work. Untouched research keeps its actual source pin. Isolated research either receives the local fix or discloses its absence.
assertions: Checks relevant changes between source revisions rather than trusting a stale report or a branch label
Does not infer deployment from a merged feature
Reconciles the returned report with the latest model and feedback before publishing
Does not overwrite revision 5 or rewrite existing receipts from the revision-4 result
Does not relabel the untouched colors report as inspected at revision B
Transfers necessary unpushed state or explicitly limits the isolated research conclusion
Refreshes affected categories without restarting all research
Preserves source revisions and unresolved limits in the approved export

evals.prompt: The open ask is 'Which of the listed metadata examples remain visible under the agreed department policy?' The saved decision maker Morgan has confirmed through the authorized review channel: 'All listed examples remain visible; protect values using the agreed ownership path.' Code research finds several metadata filters that over-hide these examples. A prior researcher speculated that each screen might need its own security policy. Review this response and propose bounded implementation work, without changing code or tickets.
evals.expected_output: The existing ask is answered using the authorized clarification and evidence. Static implementation mismatches become bounded work, not another hypothetical policy conflict. Runtime behavior remains unverified where not exercised.
assertions: Checks whether all listed examples already satisfies the exact ask and avoids asking Morgan again
Distinguishes agreed policy from code that does not implement it
Does not create screen-specific policies from implementation differences
Checks cited source paths before accepting consequential findings
Preserves the original feedback and publishes an evidence-linked answer and receipt
Proposes real dependencies and observable completion criteria while retaining agent/human/mixed planning semantics
Does not turn static analysis into a claim of demonstrated deployed failure
Carries findings into the existing JSONL without private reports, handles or a new schema

evals.prompt: The saved format question has ordinary answer, question, change and agreement feedback, plus Alex's proposal to use CSV. A receipt says the proposal was read, but there is no SME decision. Summarize readiness and export the handoff. Do not invent a decision or send notifications.
evals.expected_output: The agent interprets ordinary feedback separately and preserves the unresolved proposal. A review receipt or agreement is not SME acceptance. The export still needs review until the actual proposal lifecycle is settled.
assertions: Reads the original kinds, contexts, current model and receipts
Distinguishes ordinary answer/change/question/agree feedback from propose/adopt and accept/correct/deny
Does not settle a proposal from a review receipt alone
Preserves exact proposal wording, self-reported author and source revision
Exports the unresolved proposal ID under pending_proposal_ids and requirement needs_review
Leaves unsupported completeness or scope claims open with a named next action

evals.prompt: The reference host already recorded Alex correcting and accepting Alex's own CSV proposal at revision 2. The answer has proposal_id and acceptance_id, both evidence links, host_recorded receipts and a competing PDF proposal marked not_selected. The adapter has delivered the same notification twice. Research the encoding requirement and update it once at the existing URL. Do not ask Alex to approve the same decision again.
evals.expected_output: Research starts from the committed SME decision, preserves its immutable receipts and candidate history, and publishes only a supported requirement update. Duplicate delivery causes no second decision or follow-up.
assertions: Reads the latest publication and host_recorded receipt before acting on either notification
Treats the saved correction as already effective without agent approval or a second acceptance
Allows self-acceptance while describing the entered name as attribution rather than authentication
Preserves exact accepted text, source IDs, terminal outcomes and original host receipt times
Keeps not_selected distinct from denied
Inspects encoding evidence before changing the requirement
Rechecks the current revision before publication and avoids duplicate research effects on replay
Exports the reconciled schema-4 JSONL with both evidence links and no settled proposal in the pending list

evals.prompt: Two retention proposals were denied through the SME queue: one without feedback and one with 'one year exceeds policy'. The question is still open. A third proposal remains undecided. Another answered access question has a denied challenge. Review the lifecycle and prepare the next ask without reviving denied candidates or changing the access answer.
evals.expected_output: Both denials remain terminal with exact optional feedback. The remaining retention candidate stays unresolved; denying proposals does not answer the question. The access answer survives the denied challenge.
assertions: Checks each denial's proposal_id and host receipt instead of treating denial as a question-wide decision
Preserves the blank denial without inventing a reason
Keeps the reasoned denial and original proposal text unchanged
Leaves retention open and the third proposal pending for SME review
Preserves the existing access answer and provenance
Exports denied outcomes separately from accepted and not_selected outcomes
Routes a remaining factual or policy gap to the saved authority without unauthorized messages or tickets

evals.prompt: A reader proposed a BOM for an already accepted UTF-8 answer. They opened replacement confirmation but cancelled; no accept/correct feedback was stored. An older research report nevertheless says the answer changed. Reconcile this with the database. Then handle a later explicitly confirmed correction that did replace the answer, preserving both historical decisions.
evals.expected_output: The database distinguishes a cancelled browser interaction from a saved replacement. Research adopts only the later committed replacement, retaining the earlier answer and evidence in history.
assertions: Reads stored submissions and publications rather than treating an editor draft or research summary as a decision
Keeps the initial challenge unresolved and the existing answer intact after cancellation
Checks that the later replacement has context.replace true and links the intended proposal
Preserves earlier answer history, receipts and terminal outcomes
Does not apply the host-recorded replacement again
Carries the current exact answer and unresolved limits into the exported handoff

evals.prompt: We upgraded a questionnaire database. An old accept feedback row and delivery receipt exist, but the current question is open and that decision lacks a review receipt. The UI says 'Earlier decision — needs reviewer reconciliation'. A newer immediate denial on a different question has host_recorded receipts. Reconcile the old decision explicitly using the original evidence, preserving newer work and all original rows.
evals.expected_output: Legacy acceptance is not silently applied by migration or mistaken for a new host decision. The reviewer interprets and records its reconciliation against the current revision, leaving the newer denial untouched.
assertions: Inspects the original legacy decision, linked proposal, current question and reviews
Distinguishes delivery acknowledgement from completed interpretation
Treats the old decision as unresolved until explicit reviewer reconciliation
Verifies evidence and records a supported evidence-linked answer or a named conflict rather than blindly applying the old row
Preserves original feedback, outbox receipts, publications and new host_recorded receipts
Reconciles against the latest revision rather than overwriting newer work
Checks both the live queue and JSONL readiness after publication
Reports migration/adapter checks actually run separately from unexercised resume or harness behavior

evals.prompt: An SME save returned a network error after the host committed a corrected answer. The same UUID and body were retried after closure and succeeded. Separately, two stale tabs tried to settle one proposal; one received 409 and retained its unsent correction. Explain what actually happened using stored feedback, publications and receipts, then export the result. No production fault injection is authorized.
evals.expected_output: The audit distinguishes saved-but-unacknowledged, idempotent replay and rejected stale work. It reports one committed effect per decision, retains failed draft text without claiming it was saved, and makes no unauthorized writes.
assertions: Uses original IDs, feedback counts, publication revisions and receipts to establish committed effects
Recognizes identical UUID/body replay as success without another decision, receipt rewrite or revision
Treats the conflicting 409 correction as unsaved rather than silently resubmitting it under the latest revision
Keeps the accepted answer and terminal candidate outcomes unchanged
Does not claim a reviewer wake-up from HTTP success or receipt parsing
Exports a consistent snapshot and distinguishes executed checks from inferred or unexercised behavior
Uses disposable fixtures for any fault simulation and leaves production data untouched
